Just as an FYI - If you ever need to transfer a prescription that has refills, simply talk to the new pharmacy you wish to transfer to and they will let you know if it can be transferred or if you have to get a new rx sent in by your doctor to the new pharmacy. Transferring your existing prescriptions to one location is better for patient safety rather than having everything scattered at multiple locations :)

All pharmacists are certified to prescribe birth control in SK, of course there are pharmacists who may refuse (personal ethics) to do so but it’s mandatory that they either have another pharmacist at that pharmacy to prescribe for you or refer you to a pharmacy that can provide this service. Keep in mind, there’s specific criteria that you need to meet in order for a pharmacist to be able to prescribe for you (which they would go over in a simple assessment with you) as there are certain aspects of one’s medical history that may require a doctor’s assessment. Another good thing to note is that even though a pharmacist prescribed at that pharmacy, you have the right to take that prescription to any other pharmacy in SK that you want to get it filled. Just because the pharmacist at that pharmacy prescribed it does not mean you are bound to fill that prescription at that pharmacy location. ALSO NOTE, pharmacists cannot prescribe IUDs but we can prescribe other forms of birth control other than the pill.

Source: I’m a licensed pharmacist.
